strengths: Correctly identifies glutamatergic/excitatory cortical identity using RORB, TSHZ2, SLC22A10, FOXP2, DCC, TOX, POU6F2.
Recognizes absence of inhibitory neuronal and glial markers.
Acknowledges mixed layer-specific signals rather than overcommitting to one subtype.
weaknesses: No exact CLID mapping; raw label is broad and not ontology-resolvable.
Does not provide enough specificity for a final ontology label.

strengths: Provides an ontology-valid, more specific glutamatergic cortical neuron subtype.
Genes such as RORB, TSHZ2, SLC22A10, and GABRG1 are compatible with an IT-projection identity.
weaknesses: Over-specified: FOXP2, TOX, DCC, and POU6F2 support deep-layer/projection-associated features that are not uniquely IT.
No direct positive marker evidence distinguishes intratelencephalic projection from other glutamatergic cortical neuron subtypes.

strengths: Aligned with the dominant excitatory marker program and absence of inhibitory/glial markers.
Excitatory neuron enrichment signature supports the core identity without over-specification.
weaknesses: Broad label does not resolve layer or projection subtype.
Medium confidence because layer-discriminatory markers are incomplete.

supporting: Excitatory cortical neuron markers dominate: RORB, TSHZ2, SLC22A10, SLC22A9, SLC22A25, TPBG, PTK7, COBLL1, FOXP2, DCC, TOX, POU6F2.
Absence of canonical inhibitory (GAD1/GAD2/SST/PVALB/VIP), astrocyte, oligodendrocyte, and microglial markers.
Excitatory neuron enrichment signature (PMID 28485729) is consistent with the observed marker program.
No added hierarchical component was supported beyond CL:0000679; the IT-projection descendant CL:4023008 was not refined because the added IT component lacks direct positive support.
conflicting: In-house IT-projection specificity is not directly supported: FOXP2, TOX, DCC, POU6F2 are deep-layer/projection-associated and do not uniquely establish intratelencephalic identity.
Non-neuronal markers (CD53, FAP, DPP4, GREM2, CCDC39, CATSPERB) are present at low level and interpreted as ambient/contamination.
enrichment_or_literature: Excitatory neuron/excitatory cortical neuron enrichment from Lake et al. (PMID 28485729).

provenance.note: Publication-facing final decision, QC disposition and evaluation fields are synchronized to the submitted Supplementary Data.
